# HRP TX generator goldens

P1 frozen profile (IEEE 802.15.4a, no STS):

- 998.4 MS/s, code 9, 64 SYNC, IEEE SFD, 6.81 Mb/s, PSDU 127 B
- packet length 249280
- FCS 0x584b
- IQ golden: `../realtime_demod_golden/window.cfile` samples `[9984 : 9984+249280]`
- payload bytes: `../realtime_demod_golden/stage_payload_bytes.bin`

`pulse_48.f32` is the 48-tap real causal FIR that maps the sparse
`sampled_code` (even samples) onto `reference_preamble.bin`.  Fitted by
least squares; relative residual on one SYNC is ~3e-8.

`sts_drbg_bprf.bin` is the first 32×16 bytes of MATLAB
`allDRBG_STS.mat` (toolbox default key/nonce).  BPRF STS is
gap(512) + 32×(128 bits spread-by-8) + gap(512) chips.

## Low-tail 491.52 MS/s pulse cores

Generated by `design_tx_pulse.py` (raised-cosine spectrum at 998.4 MS/s,
f1 = passband edge, f2 = stopband edge, `minimum_phase` when requested).
Raw little-endian float32; the json sidecar carries measured metrics.
Running `python3 design_tx_pulse.py` with no arguments regenerates every
file below (the `PRESETS` table); use `--f1-mhz ...` for a one-off design.

| file | taps | phase | f1–f2 | pre 10–100 ns | post 10–100 ns | >245.76 MHz |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `pulse_trunc_linear_rc183_240.f32` | 1025 | linear-trunc | 183–240 | −28.3 dB | −28.4 dB | −59 dB |
| `pulse_minphase_rc160_240.f32` | 1025 | min | 160–240 | −56.4 dB | −16.6 dB | −72 dB |
| `pulse_linear_rc160_240.f32` | 2049 | linear | 160–240 | −38.8 dB | −38.8 dB | −137 dB |
| `pulse_minphase_rc100_215.f32` | 257 | min | 100–215 | −63.8 dB | −20.3 dB | −62 dB |
| `pulse_minphase_rc120_215.f32` | 257 | min | 120–215 | −63.6 dB | −18.2 dB | −62 dB |
| `pulse_linear_rc100_215.f32` | 513 | linear | 100–215 | −35.2 dB | −35.2 dB | −121 dB |
| `pulse_linear_rc120_215.f32` | 513 | linear | 120–215 | −37.4 dB | −37.4 dB | −120 dB |

`pulse_trunc_linear_rc183_240.f32` is the default TX pulse of the CG400 apps
(`--pulse-shape linear`, i.e. `UwbHrpPacketSource` external taps).  It is a
linear-phase RC prototype truncated so the peak sits at tap 32: −3 dB
one-sided 200 MHz (−6/−10 dB 220/232 MHz), 90/99% occupied two-sided
190/226 MHz, E2E pre/post 10–100 ns **−27.8/−27.7 dB** (post 10 dB better
than `rc160_240`; pre 30 dB worse).  The pulse group delay is 32 work taps
(16 native); the sim `/` X410 dump flow uses `--cal-delay-native 350`
(= 334 + 16) so the CIR peak stays at tap ~16, and the live SYNC template
is sliced around `pulse_center_taps()`.
`pulse_minphase_rc160_240.f32` is the min-phase predecessor (E2E
−58.0/−17.4 dB).  `rc100_215` is the narrower 157 MHz predecessor.
Untruncated linear-phase files have their peak near the middle and are
outside the radar CIR `cir_pre=16` window without calibration; kept for
offline comparison only.  Load any file with `--pulse-taps <path>`.

Do not overwrite `../uwb_radar/tx_998p4.cf32`.
